Log viewer

A command's output, however long, in a box of capped height that scrolls by itself, with long lines wrapped and error lines marked.

Status: draft

Examples

When to use it

  • For the output of a check, a setup command or a build, finished or still running, where it may run to hundreds of lines.
  • Behind a disclosure under a check list's row, or by itself on a run's screen.
  • With the error lines marked, when the app can tell them: the lines a test runner reports as failures, or the output of stderr.

When not to use it

  • For a command, a short excerpt or a file's contents. Use the code block.
  • For a change to a file. Use the diff.
  • For an agent's transcript of messages and tool calls. Use the message and the tool call in a transcript.

Accessibility

  • Use a figure. Its figcaption, ds-log-viewer__header, holds the command in a code element, ds-log-viewer__command, and ds-log-viewer__meta saying how it ended and how long it took.
  • The body, ds-log-viewer__body, takes tabindex="0" and an aria-label naming the command, so it can take focus and the arrow keys scroll it. A finished output takes role="group". It is a pre holding the output as text, or a div holding an ol, ds-log-viewer__lines, with one li, ds-log-viewer__line, per line.
  • The body caps its height at half the viewport on a phone and more on a wide screen, and scrolls by itself. Long lines wrap, so the page never scrolls sideways.
  • Mark an error line with ds-log-viewer__line--error and start it with a ds-visually-hidden span reading Error and a colon. The stylesheet tints it and draws its icon, so it is never colour alone.
  • For a failed command, open the body scrolled to its end, where the failure usually is. The app sets the scroll position.
  • Show all: when the output is longer than the box, put a quiet small button, ds-log-viewer__toggle, in ds-log-viewer__footer, with aria-expanded="false", aria-controls naming the body and a label such as Show all 46 lines. Pressing it sets aria-expanded="true" and the label Show less, and the stylesheet lifts the cap. Leave the footer out for a short output.
  • When only part of the output was kept, say so in ds-log-viewer__note inside the footer.
  • While the command runs, wrap the body and a jump-to-latest control in ds-transcript, and give the body role="log", aria-live="off" and data-ds-scroller. The body then follows new lines while the reader is at its end, and the control offers Jump to latest once they scroll up. A framework app follows by the same rule with use-transcript. Every line added is an li.
  • The component needs no script beyond that. The app sets aria-expanded and the toggle's label.
